prize_parts.citation: for exact fluctuation relations and the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, extending the second law to small systems driven far from equilibrium

statement.case_for: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality are exact, model-independent statements about driven systems arbitrarily far from equilibrium. They give the second law a precise meaning at the level of single trajectories, and they have been tested in RNA/DNA pulling, colloids in optical traps and single-electron devices. The mechanism is simple, general and rigorously analysed, and it carries across molecular biophysics, nanoscale engines and information thermodynamics. Thirty years of independent experimental confirmation make the timing unproblematic. I keep this first on scientific grounds: the opening tallies show that it is the idea I alone placed first, but support in the opening is not a measure of merit, and nothing in my colleagues' ballots addresses its substance.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness. Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Evans-Searles, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert all have strong claims, and the three-name limit forces the omission of Crooks and of Cohen, Morriss and Searles. A committee may also decide that this is a broad theoretical framework without a single decisive experiment, whereas candidates such as B007 deliver a measured result and an instrument. That is a fair worry and it is why I list B007 as my first alternative; it is also the candidate on which my colleagues are most clearly aligned, and I do not rank it low on merit (it was fifth in my opening, behind topics where I felt more directly able to judge the underlying mechanism).

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks (B007) are a textbook case of measurement that moved the frontier by orders of magnitude, with independent confirmation at the 1e-18 level and a clean two-name credit, so the recognition is timely.
responses.response: I agree on the confirmation and on the clean attribution, which is more than I can say for my own first choice. Where I qualify the argument is novelty: after the 2005 prize (combs) and the 2012 prize (ion control), the committee will have to say what is new in the citation beyond more precise clocks. The answer, that the magic-wavelength lattice removes the perturbation from the trapping light and allows many atoms to be interrogated at once, is a good physical idea, but it is an engineering of a light shift rather than the exposure of a new general mechanism. I therefore see B007 as a safe and deserving prize, and I would not object to it, but I do not accept that safety makes it the strongest scientific case.

responses.point: Circuit QED (B044) created the architecture behind most superconducting processors and is very well confirmed, though the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may make a second superconducting-circuit award too soon.
responses.response: The proximity to 2025 is a stronger objection than the opening ballots suggest, and I would weigh it more heavily than you do, since you have also noted it yourself. My other reservation is the attribution you already flag: four credited names, a 2004 theory proposal and a same-year experiment, and no principled way to choose three. I would also separate the quality of the architecture, which I do not doubt, from the question of whether it is a discovery about nature or an enabling design. Compared with B032, whose attribution problem is also hard, circuit QED has the advantage that its core results are directly reproduced everywhere, so I do not claim that my choice is cleaner on that count.

responses.point: Dynamical mean-field theory (B018) gives an exact infinite-dimensional limit of the Hubbard model and a practical route to correlated materials through DFT+DMFT, but the omission of Metzner from the credit is a real attribution risk, and agreement with experiment is uneven for specific materials.
responses.response: I recognise the appeal: the infinite-dimension limit is precisely the kind of controlled, simple mechanism that I value, and it is an exact result, which for me counts for a lot. My concern is the same one you raise. If the origin of the idea is the Metzner-Vollhardt limit and Metzner is not on the list, the three credited names do not describe the discovery fairly. I would also want evidence that the quantitative success of DFT+DMFT is more than parameter tuning in the Anderson-impurity solvers; the uneven predictive record you mention bears on whether this is a tested theory or a powerful method. I would support it if the committee finds a credit assignment that includes Metzner, which the credited-name constraint seems to preclude.

responses.point: IceCube neutrino astronomy (B012) opened a new observational window with a diffuse astrophysical flux and first source associations, a landmark instrument achievement, though credit in a thousand-person collaboration and AMANDA/Baikal precursors complicates individual attribution.
responses.response: This is a striking discovery and I take the instrument argument seriously, but I would press on both maturity and attribution. The source evidence at roughly 4 sigma for NGC 1068 and the evidence for the Galactic plane are impressive but not yet at the level of a settled population picture, and the origin of the bulk of the diffuse flux is open. On credit, I find it hard to see how the discovery analysis of the diffuse flux belongs to two or three people, and I am not convinced that Halzen and Karle are the decisive pair rather than the leaders of a collective effort. That is a problem I share with my own ballot, so I do not offer it as a decisive objection, only as a reason to prefer a candidate whose central result is already unambiguous.

uncertainties: Whether the priority history among Evans, Cohen, Morriss, Searles, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert can be settled well enough to name three laureates, and whether Seifert should be credited for stochastic thermodynamics rather than for a distinct theorem; I am recalling this history from memory and have not verified it.
Whether the committee regards a framework of exact theorems, tested by pulling and trap experiments that confirm rather than discover, as a discovery in the sense of the prize.
Whether the Nobel prize in physics for 2016 (topological defects and phases) and 2021 (complex systems) leaves room for another statistical-physics prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B032, B007 or B005. I know no credited person on the shortlist as a collaborator, and my frequent co-authors are in turbulence and population genetics. My Gothenburg colleagues on the committee (Johansson, Olsson) are in the same physics environment, but I know of no specific collaboration relevant to any ballot.
